mainTopic: Living things and טומאת אוכלין, the fat of a נפל or שליל, and a live בן תשעה found inside a slaughtered טרפה.
overview: This amud covers several topics. It opens by finishing an answer: the ברייתא about a בן פקועה is talking about a dry שחיטה, and it does not follow רבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן then says that the ruling that a living בן פקועה can get טומאת אוכלין follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. He links that view to בית שמאי, who say fish can become impure from the moment they are caught. The גמרא explains that בית הלל and רבי עקיבא differ about a flopping, dying fish. רב חסדא then asks about a fish with טרפה signs, and the question stays a תיקו. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about whether the fat of a נפל or of an unborn calf is forbidden חלב. Each side uses the ברייתא that leaves שליל fat off the מזבח. Finally, רבי אמי and רבא argue about a live בן תשעה found inside a slaughtered טרפה, and רב חסדא begins his own statement on that case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is a dry slaughter, not following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is explained as a case where the mother's שחיטה released no blood. It also does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a dry slaughter, and the ברייתא does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question on the ברייתא. It says the mother was slaughtered without any blood coming out, and the ברייתא does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the בן פקועה would need a separate הכשר, such as passing through a river. If blood came out at the mother's שחיטה, that blood should already have wet it and made it susceptible. In a dry שחיטה there was no liquid at all, so it still needs a separate הכשר. רבי שמעון holds that the שחיטה itself makes the meat susceptible, even with no liquid. The ברייתא cannot follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter
Dry, meaning no blood came out
And this does not follow the view of

phrases.english: With a dry slaughter,
phrases.notes: No blood came out when the mother was slaughtered, so nothing wet the meat to make it susceptible to impurity.

phrases.english: and it is not like רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁחִיטָה יַבִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier question on the ברייתא, which was asked before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a dry שחיטה, plus saying which תנא the ברייתא does not follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood from the mother's שחיטה should already have made the בן פקועה susceptible.
steps.terutzMaskana: No blood came out, and the ברייתא does not follow רבי שמעון, so a separate הכשר is still needed.

steps.title: Who taught that a living בן פקועה can become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a grown-up בן פקועה becomes susceptible in a river and impure in a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught: it passed through a river and became susceptible, then went to a cemetery and became impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows. The ברייתא treats a living, walking בן פקועה as food that can get impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising part is that the animal is alive and walking around. Even so, the ברייתא says it can get food-impurity once it is wet. Normally we think living things are not "food" for impurity purposes. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא taught this? (asking whose view a teaching follows)
It became susceptible to impurity, by getting wet
Cemetery, a source of impurity
It became impure

phrases.english: Who is the תנא who taught:
It passed through a river, so it became susceptible;
phrases.notes: "It" is a בן פקועה that grew up and is walking around alive. The river water is what makes it susceptible.

phrases.english: it went to a cemetery, so it became impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the case to asking whose opinion the ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a living בן פקועה can receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it is רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds a living בן פקועה gets food-impurity after הכשר, while the חכמים say nothing alive can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is רבי יוסי הגלילי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said in his name: it can become impure with food-impurity, but it needs הכשר. The חכמים say: it cannot become impure with food-impurity, because it is alive, and anything alive cannot become impure with food-impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. He backs this up with a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי treats the living בן פקועה as food. That is because it can be eaten without its own שחיטה, so it only needs to get wet. The חכמים hold a basic rule: anything alive is not food for impurity purposes, even if it may be eaten. That is why the river-and-cemetery ברייתא can only follow רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity that food can receive
Becoming susceptible to impurity by contact with liquid
Alive

steps.whyThisMatters: The חכמים's rule, that nothing alive gets טומאת אוכלין, is the main principle this whole section is arguing about.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
It is the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says
in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי:
It can become impure with the impurity of food,
phrases.notes: "It" is the living בן פקועה.

phrases.english: but it needs הכשר.
But the Sages say:
It cannot become impure with the impurity of food,
because it is alive,
and anything that is alive
cannot become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who the תנא is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds a living בן פקועה receives טומאת אוכלין once it has הכשר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי agree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן is following his own view elsewhere. There he said רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן said: רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's answer fits another statement of his. This sets up the next step, which shows where each of the two opinions is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי hold that something still alive can receive טומאת אוכלין. So רבי יוחנן's answer here is not new. It matches his general view that these two opinions are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: And he goes (follows)
According to his own reasoning; consistent with his other statement
One thing, meaning the same idea

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning,
for רבי יוחנן said:
רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי
said the same thing.
phrases.notes: Both hold that something still alive can get food-impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבי יוחנן's answer to another statement of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי share one view: a living thing can receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: The sources: the ברייתא and the משנה about fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is the ברייתא just quoted. בית שמאי's view is from a משנה: fish can receive impurity from when they are caught. בית הלל say from when they die, and רבי עקיבא says from when they can no longer live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי: what we just said. בית שמאי: as we learned in a משנה: From when can fish receive impurity? בית שמאי say: from when they are caught. בית הלל say: from when they die. רבי עקיבא says: from when they can no longer live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where each opinion comes from. רבי יוסי הגלילי's is the ברייתא we just saw. בית שמאי's is a משנה about fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish do not need שחיטה, so once they are caught they are ready to eat. בית שמאי say they count as food for impurity right then, even while still alive, just like רבי יוסי הגלילי says about the living בן פקועה. בית הלל wait until the fish dies, which matches the חכמים's rule. רבי עקיבא takes a middle position: once the fish is too far gone to survive.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we said (already quoted above)
Fish
Able to receive impurity
From when they are caught
From when they die
They are unable to stay alive

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on whether something living can get food-impurity. רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי say yes, once it is ready to eat. The חכמים and בית הלל say no, only after death. רבי עקיבא says from when it can no longer survive.
steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not saying fish are dead when caught. Their point is that a fish counts as food for impurity even while still alive.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי הגלילי: that is what we just said.
בית שמאי: as we learned in a משנה:
Fish: from when can they receive impurity?
בית שמאי say: from when they are caught,
and בית הלל say: from when they die.
רבי עקיבא says:
from the time that they can no longer live.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources behind רבי יוחנן's claim that the two views match.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי and בית שמאי hold the same view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא quoted above, and the משנה about fish (עוקצין 3:8)

steps.title: What is the practical difference between בית הלל and רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case would separate בית הלל's view from רבי עקיבא's view about when fish become able to receive impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה just quoted and asks when בית הלל and רבי עקיבא would actually rule differently. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say 'from when they die,' and רבי עקיבא says 'from when they can no longer live.' Those sound almost the same, so the גמרא wants a real case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? A request for the practical case where two opinions differ.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means בית הלל and רבי עקיבא from the משנה about fish in the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between two opinions in the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'from when they die' and 'from when they can no longer live' give different results.

steps.title: The difference is a flopping, dying fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the difference is a fish that is convulsing: still moving, but sure to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The difference between them is a convulsing fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: they disagree about a fish that is flopping around and dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flopping fish is not dead yet, so for בית הלל it cannot yet become impure. But it can no longer live, so for רבי עקיבא it already can.

keyTerms.meaning: A convulsing fish: still twitching, but dying.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל need the fish to be actually dead; רבי עקיבא is satisfied once it can no longer survive, like a flopping fish.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A convulsing fish is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דָּג מְקַרְטֵעַ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A convulsing fish: impure-capable for רבי עקיבא, not yet for בית הלל.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks about a fish with טרפה signs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks: if a fish develops signs of a טרפה, is it treated as 'no longer able to live'? The question can be asked on either side of the debate about whether a טרפה can survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked: If signs of a טרפה developed in fish, what is the law? You can ask it according to the one who says a טרפה can live, and you can ask it according to the one who says a טרפה cannot live.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא raises a new question building on רבי עקיבא's view. The גמרא says the question works for both opinions about whether a טרפה can live, and it explains this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, what matters is 'can it still live?' A fish with a fatal-type injury like a טרפה might count as already unable to live, even though it is swimming normally. The question is whether טרפה signs put a fish into that category.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a dilemma: a real question the speaker does not know the answer to.
Signs of a טרפה: injuries or defects that make an animal a טרפה.
A טרפה can live: the view that a טרפה does not necessarily die soon.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked:
If signs of a tereifa developed in fish, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking within רבי עקיבא's view: does this fish count as 'no longer able to live,' so it can already become impure?

phrases.english: Ask it according to the one who says a tereifa can live,

phrases.aramaic: וְתִיבְּעֵי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה אֵינָהּ חַיָּה.
phrases.english: and ask it according to the one who says a tereifa cannot live.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב חִסְדָּא: נוֹלְדוּ בְּדָגִים סִימָנֵי טְרֵפָה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי עקיבא's 'can no longer live' standard, now clarified by the flopping fish, and applies it to a fish with טרפה signs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a fish with טרפה signs counts as unable to live, so it can already receive impurity.

steps.title: Why the question works on both sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: even if a טרפה animal can live, maybe a weak fish cannot. And even if a טרפה animal is treated as dead, maybe that only applies to animals that need שחיטה, not fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the one who says a טרפה can live: maybe that is only an animal, which has strong life, but fish, whose life is not strong, would not survive. Or maybe even according to the one who says a טרפה cannot live, that is only an animal, whose kind has שחיטה, but fish, whose kind has no שחיטה, I would say not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why רב חסדא's question is open on both sides of the טרפה debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the view that a טרפה can live may hold only for strong animals, so a weaker fish with טרפה signs would be seen as dying, and it could become impure. Side two: the view that a טרפה is treated as dead may be tied to animals that need שחיטה, so a fish, which needs no שחיטה, would not be seen as dead. So neither opinion settles the fish case automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: Its life force is strong.
Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a dilemma.
Its kind requires שחיטה to be permitted.

phrases.english: Ask it according to the one who says a tereifa can live:
maybe that is an animal, whose life force is strong,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּגִים דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא חַיּוּתַיְיהוּ – לָא,
phrases.english: but fish, whose life force is not strong, would not survive,
or perhaps, even according to the one who says
a tereifa cannot live,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּהֵמָה דְּיֵשׁ בְּמִינָהּ שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: that applies to an animal, whose kind requires slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּגִים דְּאֵין בְּמִינָן שְׁחִיטָה – אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: but fish, whose kind does not require slaughter, I would say not.
phrases.notes: On this side, the fish is not treated as dead, so it cannot yet become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה חַיָּה, בְּהֵמָה הוּא דִּנְפִישָׁא חַיּוּתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two-sided framing given briefly in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the differences between fish and animals (weaker life, no שחיטה) change how טרפה signs are treated.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב חסדא's question with תיקו: it stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer to רב חסדא's question, so it is left unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides from the last step are reasonable, and no source decides between them. So the status of a fish with טרפה signs stays in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a fish with טרפה signs can already receive impurity under רבי עקיבא's view is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dilemma of steps 8-9 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about a fish with טרפה signs remains unresolved.

steps.title: Is the fat of a נפל like an animal's fat or a wild animal's fat?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: if an animal gives birth to a non-viable newborn, רבי יוחנן says its fat is like the forbidden fat of a בהמה, and ריש לקיש says it is like the permitted fat of a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an animal expelled a נפל: רבי יוחנן said its fat is like the fat of a domesticated animal, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש said its fat is like the fat of an undomesticated animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about a newborn that cannot survive, and presents a dispute about its fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat of a domesticated animal (חלב בהמה) is forbidden, while fat of an undomesticated animal (חלב חיה) is permitted. רבי יוחנן treats the נפל's fat like a normal animal's, so it is forbidden. ריש לקיש compares it to a חיה's fat, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-viable newborn that cannot survive.
Fat of a domesticated animal, which is forbidden to eat.
Fat of an undomesticated animal, which is permitted.

steps.confusionAlert: The word חַיָּה changes meaning here. In the last steps, 'טרפה חיה' meant 'a טרפה can LIVE.' Here 'חלב חיה' means the fat of a WILD ANIMAL like a deer.

phrases.english: If it expelled a non-viable newborn,
phrases.notes: 'It' means a mother animal, such as a cow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
its fat is like the fat of a domesticated animal,
phrases.notes: So it is forbidden, like normal animal fat.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
its fat is like the fat of an undomesticated animal.
phrases.notes: So it is permitted, since the fat of a deer or similar animal is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵטִילָה נֵפֶל, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חֶלְבּוֹ כְּחֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו closed the fish discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a נפל's fat is forbidden like a בהמה's fat. ריש לקיש: it is permitted like a חיה's fat.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side: the air or the months
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the fat is forbidden because coming out into the air makes it a real animal. ריש לקיש says it is permitted because only finishing the months makes it a real animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: its fat is like the fat of a בהמה, because going out into the air is what counts. ריש לקיש said: its fat is like the fat of a חיה, because finishing the months is what counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the two opinions from Step 11 and now adds the reason behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, once the young animal comes out into the world, it is its own בהמה, so its חלב is forbidden even though it was not viable. For ריש לקיש, a young animal only counts as its own animal if it finished its full months of pregnancy. This one did not, so its fat is permitted, just like the fat of a חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, 'the air causes': being born into the open world makes it its own animal
'The months cause': finishing the full pregnancy makes it its own animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Its fat is like the fat of a domestic animal,
because the air causes it.
phrases.notes: He means that coming out into the open air of the world is what makes it count as its own animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Its fat is like the fat of a wild animal,
because the months cause it.
phrases.notes: Only finishing the full months of pregnancy makes it a real animal, and this one never did.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חֶלְבּוֹ כְּחֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה – אַוֵּירָא גָּרֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the dispute from Step 11 and adds the reasoning for each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: birth into the air makes it a בהמה, so its fat is forbidden. ריש לקיש: only completed months make it a בהמה, so its fat is permitted.

steps.title: Second version: everyone agrees an underdeveloped young animal is nothing
steps.stepSummary: A second version says that if the months were not finished, everyone agrees it does not count as an animal at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: wherever its months were not finished, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the argument. First it tells us what both sides agree on, and this sets up where they really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the non-viable young animal from Step 12 is not argued about at all. Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree its fat is not forbidden, because it never finished its months. So the real argument must be somewhere else, which the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: Its months were completed: a full-term pregnancy
It is nothing: it does not count as an animal at all

steps.confusionAlert: In this second version, רבי יוחנן agrees that the non-viable young animal's fat is not forbidden. The two versions disagree about which case they are even arguing over.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא כָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו –
phrases.english: Wherever its months were not completed,
it is nothing.
phrases.notes: Both sides agree here: its fat is not counted as forbidden חלב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא כָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version that removes the non-viable young animal from the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the months of pregnancy were not completed, all agree it is not an animal, so its fat is not forbidden.

steps.title: Where they argue: fat taken from a live full-term calf still inside its mother
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about a live nine-month calf whose fat someone pulled out of the mother and ate. רבי יוחנן says months alone make it a בהמה. ריש לקיש says it needs both months and birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is when someone put his hand inside an animal, pulled off fat from a live nine-month calf, and ate it. רבי יוחנן said its fat is like בהמה fat, because the months are what count. ריש לקיש said its fat is like חיה fat, because it needs both the months and going out into the air.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the second version, the גמרא shows the exact case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the calf finished its nine months but was never born. For רבי יוחנן, finishing the months is enough, so its fat is forbidden even before birth. For ריש לקיש, it needs both full months and birth into the air, so this fat is still permitted. Notice that רבי יוחנן's reason flipped from 'the air' (Step 12) to 'the months' in this version.

keyTerms.meaning: When they argue: where the real disagreement is
The womb (literally 'insides') of the animal
A nine-month calf: full-term
He pulled off or tore out

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: they argue about a non-viable young animal that was born (air vs. months). Version 2: they argue about a full-term calf still inside its mother (months alone vs. months plus air).

phrases.english: Where they argue
is where one put his hand into the womb of an animal

phrases.aramaic: וְתָלַשׁ חֵלֶב שֶׁל בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי וְאָכַל.
phrases.english: and pulled off fat of a live nine-month calf and ate it.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Its fat is like the fat of a domestic animal; the months cause it.
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Its fat is like the fat of a wild animal;
the months and the air together cause it.
phrases.notes: For him, it needs both: full months and actually being born.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי – הֵיכָא דְּהוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ לִמְעֵי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version by identifying the real case of dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Full-term calf still inside its mother: רבי יוחנן says its fat is forbidden (months alone). ריש לקיש says its fat is permitted (needs months and birth).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש: why would the Torah need to exclude unborn fat from the altar?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the fat of a שליל is excluded from the fats offered on the מזבח. רבי יוחנן argues this exclusion only makes sense if that fat would otherwise count as real חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: Just as the fat and two kidneys said about the אשם leave out a שליל, so too for every קרבן, a שליל is left out. Now, according to me it makes sense that a verse was needed to exclude it. But according to you, why was a verse needed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא and uses it to attack ריש לקיש's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the אשם that the fat of an unborn calf is not part of the fats offered on the מזבח, and applies this to all קרבנות. רבי יוחנן says: I hold that this fat is real forbidden חלב, so a verse was needed to tell us not to offer it. But if, as ריש לקיש says, it is not real חלב at all, why would the Torah bother to exclude it?

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering: always a male animal
The two kidneys, offered on the מזבח with the fat
An unborn calf still inside its mother
'It works out fine': this makes sense according to one view, setting up a challenge to the other
A verse was needed to exclude it

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about which fats go on the מזבח, not about eating. רבי יוחנן's point is that the Torah only needs to exclude something that would otherwise have been included.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
Just as the fat and the two kidneys
that are mentioned with the guilt offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:3–4

phrases.english: leave out an unborn calf,
phrases.notes: Literally, 'a שליל is taken out of the rule.' Its fat is not part of what gets offered.

phrases.english: so too for every offering, an unborn calf is left out.
It works out fine according to me:
that is why a verse was needed to exclude it.
But according to you, why was it needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from Step 14 (and 12) using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the fat of a שליל is not real forbidden חלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse is only needed to exclude something that would otherwise be included. If שליל fat is not real חלב, there is nothing to exclude, so the verse would be pointless.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: that same verse is my source
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the verse excluding שליל fat is exactly where he learns that this fat is not real חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: my reason also comes from here.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers רבי יוחנן's challenge by turning the verse into support for his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן read the verse as proof that שליל fat needed to be excluded. ריש לקיש reads it the other way: the verse tells us that the fat of a שליל is not counted as real חלב at all. So the verse is not extra; it is the very source of his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: My reason: the source of my opinion
From here: from this very verse

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same verse. רבי יוחנן says it shows שליל fat had to be excluded. ריש לקיש says it is the source that שליל fat is not real חלב.

phrases.english: He said to him:
My reason also comes from here.
phrases.notes: He means the verse itself is what teaches that the fat of an unborn calf is not real forbidden חלב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דִּידִי נָמֵי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by reading the same verse as his own source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the verse as the source of the challenged view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seems useless for ריש לקיש, since it excludes something that is not חלב anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is exactly what teaches that שליל fat is not real חלב, so it is the basis of ריש לקיש's view.

steps.title: Second version: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from the guilt-offering ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, ריש לקיש uses the ברייתא excluding שליל fat from the מזבח to attack רבי יוחנן. If this fat is real חלב, why can't it be offered?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went the other way. ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן with the ברייתא: 'Just as with the fat and two kidneys of the אשם, a fetus's fat is excluded, so too with every offering, a fetus's fat is excluded.' ריש לקיש said: 'For me it makes sense. The Torah left it out because it is not real חלב. But for you, who say it is real חלב, it should be offered!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same argument from step 15. This time ריש לקיש is the one asking, and he uses the ברייתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבי יוחנן used the ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש. Here the roles are flipped. ריש לקיש says the Torah left out שליל fat from the מזבח because it is not real חלב. If רבי יוחנן says it is real חלב, then it should be offered like any other חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: Taken out of the category, excluded
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא as step 15, but used in the opposite direction. In this version, ריש לקיש is attacking רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
Just as the fat and the two kidneys
that are stated regarding the guilt offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:3–4

phrases.english: a fetus is excluded from the category,
so too with all offerings, a fetus is excluded from the category.
Granted, according to me,
that is why the Merciful One excluded it,
but according to you, let it be offered?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the steps 15–16 exchange, with the roles reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that שליל fat is real חלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fat is real חלב, it should go on the מזבח. The Torah leaving it out shows it is not real חלב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: it is like an animal too young to offer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the fat can be real חלב and still not be offered. It is like a מחוסר זמן, an animal too young to be brought as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: It is just like an animal whose time has not yet come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself. He says that not being offered on the מזבח does not prove the fat is not real חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר זמן is a real animal of a kind that can be offered, but it still cannot be offered until it is old enough. In the same way, שליל fat can be real forbidden חלב and still be left out of the מזבח. So the ברייתא does not prove ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal lacking time; too young (under eight days) to be offered
It is just like; a comparison to a known case

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is just like an animal that is lacking time.
phrases.notes: He means an animal under eight days old, which cannot yet be offered. ויקרא 22:27

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמְּחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (מידי דהוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If something is excluded from the מזבח, it must not be real חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Something can be fully in its category and still be unfit for the מזבח, like a מחוסר זמן. So שליל fat can be real חלב.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the ברייתא about שליל fat can be read to fit either side. רבי יוחנן's answer is that being kept off the מזבח does not mean the fat is not real חלב.

steps.title: רבי אמי: a live nine-month fetus inside a slaughtered טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that if you slaughter a טרפה and find a live nine-month fetus inside, the positions flip. The one who usually forbids (רבי מאיר) permits it, and the one who usually permits (the חכמים) forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: If someone slaughters a טרפה and finds a live nine-month fetus inside it, then according to the one who forbids, it is permitted, and according to the one who permits, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's argument about a live בן תשעה found in a slaughtered animal. רבי אמי applies it to a new case: the mother is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the fetus needs its own שחיטה, so it stands on its own. Because of this, the mother being a טרפה does not affect it, and its own שחיטה permits it. The חכמים say the mother's שחיטה permits the fetus, so it is tied to its mother. When the mother is a טרפה, the fetus is forbidden along with her.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which שחיטה cannot make kosher
A live fetus that has finished nine months
The one who forbids (here, רבי מאיר)
The one who permits (here, the חכמים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The one who forbids' and 'the one who permits' describe each side's view in the regular case of a kosher mother. In this טרפה case, their rulings come out the opposite way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
One who slaughters a tereifa
and found inside it a live nine-month fetus,
according to the one who forbids, he permits;
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר from the משנה, who requires the fetus to have its own שחיטה.

phrases.english: according to the one who permits, he forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה's argument about a live בן תשעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a slaughtered טרפה, רבי מאיר permits the live בן תשעה through its own שחיטה, while the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: רבא: even the חכמים permit it, because of four סימנים
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי אמי. He says that even the חכמים permit the fetus, because the Torah made four סימנים valid for it: the mother's and its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: According to the one who permits, it is also permitted. The Merciful One made four סימנים valid for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the second half of רבי אמי's statement. He says that even the חכמים would permit this fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי thought that for the חכמים, the fetus depends only on its mother. רבא says the Torah gave this fetus four valid סימנים: the mother's two and its own two. So when the mother's שחיטה cannot help because she is a טרפה, the fetus's own שחיטה still permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and food pipe that are cut in שחיטה
Made valid, made fit

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי: in a טרפה mother, the חכמים forbid the fetus. רבא: they permit it through its own שחיטה, because the Torah made four סימנים valid for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that, for the חכמים, a fetus can be permitted either through its mother's שחיטה or through its own.

phrases.english: Rava said:
according to the one who permits, it is also permitted,
the Merciful One made four simanim valid for it.
phrases.notes: He means the mother's two סימנים plus the fetus's own two. Cutting either pair works.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּתִּיר נָמֵי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבי אמי's ruling in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the חכמים forbid the fetus. רבא agrees with רבי אמי about רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אמי assumed the fetus can only be permitted through its mother. In fact, the Torah made four סימנים valid for it, so its own שחיטה also works.

steps.title: רב חסדא sets up the case of a live fetus inside a slaughtered טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא begins a statement about someone who slaughtered a טרפה and found a live nine-month fetus inside it. His ruling has not come yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If someone slaughters a טרפה and finds inside it a live nine-month fetus...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב חסדא describes the same case רבי אמי and רבא just discussed, and his ruling will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same one from step 19: the mother is a טרפה, and her nine-month fetus is alive inside her. רבי אמי and רבא already disagreed about it. Now a third אמורא, רב חסדא, gives his own view on it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters an animal with kosher שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the opening of רב חסדא's statement. Don't look for his ruling here, because it comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
One who slaughtered a tereifa
and found inside it a live nine-month-old fetus,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה, וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אמי and רבא disagreed about the case in steps 19-20, רב חסדא opens his own statement on the same case. His ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the case is set up here: a live nine-month fetus is found inside a slaughtered טרפה. The ruling follows in the next line.
